From 05fe3c103f7e6b8b4fca8a7001dfc9ed4628085b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2022 14:47:52 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mm/usercopy: return 1 from hardened_usercopy __setup()
 handler

__setup() handlers should return 1 if the command line option is handled
and 0 if not (or maybe never return 0; it just pollutes init's
environment).  This prevents:

  Unknown kernel command line parameters \
  "BOOT_IMAGE=/boot/bzImage-517rc5 hardened_usercopy=off", will be \
  passed to user space.

  Run /sbin/init as init process
   with arguments:
     /sbin/init
   with environment:
     HOME=/
     TERM=linux
     BOOT_IMAGE=/boot/bzImage-517rc5
     hardened_usercopy=off
or
     hardened_usercopy=on
but when "hardened_usercopy=foo" is used, there is no Unknown kernel
command line parameter.

Return 1 to indicate that the boot option has been handled.
Print a warning if strtobool() returns an error on the option string,
but do not mark this as in unknown command line option and do not cause
init's environment to be polluted with this string.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20220222034249.14795-1-rdunlap@infradead.org
Link: lore.kernel.org/r/64644a2f-4a20-bab3-1e15-3b2cdd0defe3@omprussia.ru
Fixes: b5cb15d9372ab ("usercopy: Allow boot cmdline disabling of hardening")
Signed-off-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Reported-by: Igor Zhbanov <i.zhbanov@omprussia.ru>
Acked-by: Chris von Recklinghausen <crecklin@redhat.com>
Cc: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/usercopy.c b/mm/usercopy.c
index e7b0cb49daa1..bf4d57fefee1 100644
--- a/mm/usercopy.c
+++ b/mm/usercopy.c
@@ -284,7 +284,10 @@ static bool enable_checks __initdata = true;
 
 static int __init parse_hardened_usercopy(char *str)
 {
-	return strtobool(str, &enable_checks);
+	if (strtobool(str, &enable_checks))
+		pr_warn("Invalid option string for hardened_usercopy: '%s'\n",
+			str);
+	return 1;
 }
 
 __setup("hardened_usercopy=", parse_hardened_usercopy);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `mm/usercopy.c`**
   - The function `parse_hardened_usercopy` was modified to:
     - Print a warning message if `strtobool` returns an error when parsing the option string.
     - Always return `1` to indicate that the command line option has been handled, regardless of the validity of the input string.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the `parse_hardened_usercopy` function ensures that any command line option related to `hardened_usercopy` is acknowledged (returns `1`), preventing pollution of the init environment with unrecognized parameters. This addresses the issue of unknown kernel command line parameters being passed to user space, as highlighted in the patch description. The warning mechanism provides feedback on invalid input without affecting the overall handling of the command line options.

mm/usercopy: return 1 from hardened_usercopy __setup()

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `parse_hardened_usercopy` function not returning a value indicating that the command line option was handled when an invalid option string was provided. This led to unknown kernel command line parameters being passed to user space, which polluted the init environment. The function should have returned `1` to signify that the option was processed, regardless of its validity.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int __init parse_hardened_usercopy(char *str)
 {
-	return strtobool(str, &enable_checks);
+	if (strtobool(str, &enable_checks))
+		pr_warn("Invalid option string for hardened_usercopy: '%s'\n",
+			str);
+	return 1;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
return strtobool(str, &enable_checks);
```
Reason:
The `parse_hardened_usercopy` function was returning the result of `strtobool`, which could be `0` (indicating failure) when an invalid option string was provided. This caused the function to not signal that the command line option was handled, leading to unknown kernel command line parameters being passed to user space and polluting the init environment.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (strtobool(str, &enable_checks))
    pr_warn("Invalid option string for hardened_usercopy: '%s'\n", str);
return 1;
```
Reason:
The patch modifies the function to always return `1`, indicating that the command line option has been processed, regardless of its validity. It also adds a warning message if `strtobool` fails, ensuring that the invalid option is logged without affecting the init environment.
